viewsWelcome.contents:
Open an ACH file (.ach, .nacha, or a text file that starts with an ACH file header) to see its batches, entries and addenda here.
[Open Sample File](command:achAtlas.openSample)
[Open Sample File With Problems](command:achAtlas.openSampleProblems)
[Getting Started Guide](command:achAtlas.openWalkthrough)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with ACH Atlas
walkthroughs.description: Open a sample ACH file, read every field in a hover, find problems with their codes, follow the totals and try the Pro tools in the free 14-day trial.

steps.title: Open a sample file
steps.description:
ACH Atlas reads ACH files: 94-character records for the file header, batches, entries, addenda and controls. Open the invented sample to follow along, or open one of your own files.
[Open Sample File](command:achAtlas.openSample)

steps.title: Read the outline and hover a field
steps.description:
The ACH Atlas view lists the batches with their entries and totals. Rest the pointer on any field to see its name, positions, raw value and meaning: amounts with their cents, dates with the weekday, routing numbers with the check digit.
[Show the Outline](command:workbench.view.extension.achAtlas)

steps.title: Find problems
steps.description:
Open the sample with problems: a shortened record, a wrong check digit, an invalid date and a wrong entry hash appear in the Problems view, each with a code and a message that says what was expected.
[Open Sample File With Problems](command:achAtlas.openSampleProblems)
[Check Current File](command:achAtlas.checkFile)

steps.title: Follow the totals
steps.description:
The status bar shows the field at the cursor and the totals of the file, computed from the entries. Go To Batch jumps to a batch; Show File Totals lists every batch.
[Show File Totals](command:achAtlas.showTotals)
[Go To Batch](command:achAtlas.goToBatch)

steps.title: Try the Pro tools (14-day trial)
steps.description:
Create a test file with correct totals, anonymise a file before you share it, recompute the control records, compare two files or report on a folder. The first Pro command starts a free 14-day trial on this computer; no key, account or network is needed.
[Create Test File](command:achAtlas.generate)
[Recompute Control Records And Padding](command:achAtlas.fixControls)
[Show Licence Status](command:achAtlas.licenceStatus)

achAtlas.maxFileSizeMB.markdownDescription: Largest file, in megabytes, that is checked automatically and gets hovers, the outline and symbols. Larger files are checked on demand with **ACH Atlas: Check Current File**.

achAtlas.maxProblems.markdownDescription: Largest number of problems listed per file.

achAtlas.validateOnType.markdownDescription: Check ACH files while you type (after a short pause). Files above 2 MB are checked when opened and saved.

achAtlas.hover.enabled.markdownDescription: Show the field name, positions, raw value and meaning when the pointer rests on a field.

achAtlas.detectPlainText.markdownDescription: Switch plain text files (for example `.txt` or `.dat`) to the ACH language when their first record is an ACH file header.

achAtlas.checks.effectiveDate.markdownDescription: Report effective entry dates that lie before the file creation date, more than 60 days after it, or on a weekend. Invalid dates are always reported.

achAtlas.checks.blocking.markdownDescription: Report files whose record count is not a multiple of ten (missing or extra filler records of nines). Turn off when your bank accepts files without filler.

achAtlas.reconcile.include.markdownDescription: Glob pattern of the files that the folder commands (**Create Reconciliation Report For A Folder**, **Anonymise Folder**) read. Files that do not start with an ACH file header are skipped.

achAtlas.reconcile.maxFiles.markdownDescription: Largest number of files the folder commands read.

achAtlas.export.neutraliseFormulas.markdownDescription: Put an apostrophe in front of CSV cells that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (a value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return). Turn off only when a program that reads the CSV needs the exact values.
